title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 8-10). Grothendieck is axiomatising an 'Algèbre des figures' for analysis situs, a combinatorial and 'tame' (modéré) foundation for stratified spaces. Several sets are in play: 𝔉, the figures, with least element φ (the empty figure); 𝔐, a distinguished subset of figures (from p.10, the strata, since 'F est une strate de G' means F ∈ 𝔐 and F ≤ G); and ℒ, the lieux. On 𝔉 there are several relations: ≤ (inclusion), ≪ (on p.10 tied to the 'déploiement' F ↦ F̃ and to incidence), ≾ (refinement), compatibility and disjunction. Previous page: two figures are disjoint iff their inf is φ in a strong sense (1.13). That is, their sets of lieux ouvt(F) and ouvt(G) are disjoint as sets, and every lieu of one is compatible with (disjoint from) every lieu of the other. Disjoint implies compatible. In the set-theoretic model both relations are trivial on lieux: lieux are always compatible, and disjoint iff distinct. But even in the set-theoretic, tame case, compatibility on 𝔐 is non-trivial.

This page makes four points.
(i) Compatibility on 𝔐 is an important relation that adds to ≤_𝔐 and ≪_𝔐.
(ii) Reconstruction claim, stated as 'moralement': the atlas is recovered up to unique isomorphism from the structure (𝔐, ≤, ≪, compatibility). A margin note suggests that disjunction might be the better third relation. In modern terms, the stratified object is determined by a poset of strata carrying a second order (incidence or closure) and a symmetric binary relation (compatibility, or orthogonality).
(iii) Notation: F ∥ G (1.14) for disjunction, and F ◇ G or a circled 'bow-tie' symbol F ≬ G (1.15) for compatibility. The bow-tie is faster to write but less suggestive of the combinatorial idea.
(iv) The refinement relation ≾ on 𝔉 is announced as formally the most delicate notion and the one most specific to the algebra of figures. Its geometric meaning is to be explained by examples, which the next page starts on. That page lists alternative base structures on 𝔉 ({≤,≪}, {≤,≾}, {≪, 𝔉→P(𝔉)}). It then revises, on 20 June, to a geometric characterisation of ≪ through the incidence relation ◁ ('F est une strate de G').

The problem served is to find a minimal combinatorial datum (orders plus a compatibility or orthogonality relation on strata) from which a tame stratified space or atlas can be reconstructed. This belongs to the programme of 'topologie modérée' in the Esquisse.
errors: The reconstruction statement is explicitly heuristic ('Moralement'); no proof or precise hypotheses are given on this page.

There is an internal hesitation over which relation suffices, compatibility or disjunction (margin 'ou mieux ... la disjonction'). By (1.13), disjunction on figures is expressible via ≤ and compatibility on lieux, so the two choices are not obviously equivalent on 𝔐 alone.

Possible slip: on p.8 the transcription says 'tout lieu de l'une est disjoint ... de tout lieu de l'autre' while (1.13) says 'compatible'. The definitions of compatibility versus disjunction on lieux need care. The page does not resolve this.

ideas.what: Compatibility relation on the set of strata 𝔐 as an essential extra datum beyond the order relations ≤ and ≪
ideas.modern_name: coherence or conflict relation on a poset (cf. event structures, coherence spaces, face-poset data of regular cell complexes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nielsen-Plotkin-Winskel (event structures, 1981); Girard (coherence spaces, 1987); in combinatorial topology, face posets à la Björner
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 discusses tame topology only programmatically; this relational formalism is unpublished as far as I know

ideas.what: Claim that an atlas is recovered up to unique isomorphism from (𝔐, ≤, ≪, compatibility or disjunction)
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial reconstruction of a stratified space or CW complex from its (enriched) face or stratum poset; exit-path or entrance-path poset reconstruction
ideas.usually_credited_to: regular CW complexes from face posets (folklore; Björner 1984); stratified homotopy via posets (MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie, later)
ideas.where_published: unsure; not in Esquisse in this form

ideas.what: Notations F ∥ G (disjunction) and F ◇ G / circled bow-tie (compatibility)
Refinement relation ≾ on figures as the most specific notion of the 'Algèbre des figures'
ideas.modern_name: refinement (subdivision) order on stratifications or triangulations
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical PL topology (subdivision); o-minimal cell decomposition refinement (van den Dries et al.)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions tame structures and dévissage of stratified spaces but not this relational axiomatics

missed.claim: Grothendieck's structure (poset of strata with order(s) plus a symmetric compatibility or disjunction relation, from which the whole atlas is recovered) closely parallels the contemporaneous theoretical-computer-science notion of event structures and prime algebraic domains. There, a poset plus a symmetric conflict relation determines a domain of configurations. It also parallels Girard's coherence spaces (1987). No link between Grothendieck's tame-topology axiomatics and these structures appears in the literature.
missed.quote: pour récupérer l'atlas (à iso unique près) il suffit de connaître sur M ces deux relations d'ordre, et la relation de compatibilité
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests that stratified or tame spaces could be presented by 'event-structure-like' combinatorial data. That could link stratified homotopy theory (exit-path categories) with domain-theoretic reconstruction results. The parallel is formal only.

missed.claim: There is a precise reconstruction theorem to be stated and proved: which axioms on (𝔐, ≤, ≪, compatibility) characterise the 'atlases' of the Algèbre des figures, together with an equivalence of categories.
missed.quote: Moralement, pour récupérer l'atlas (à iso unique près) il suffit de connaître sur M ces deux relations d'ordre, et la relation de compatibilité.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A combinatorial presentation of tame stratified spaces is still sought; compare o-minimal triangulation and the combinatorics of stratified spaces in exit-path ∞-categories.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly notation and a heuristic claim. The notable point is an unpublished relational axiomatics for tame stratified spaces, with a reconstruction claim from an order plus compatibility structure on strata. It is an interesting but unproven sketch and fits the known Esquisse programme.
transcription_corrections: (1.15): the first alternative symbol is a diamond with a vertical stroke inside (◇ with a bar), and the second is a crossed 'bow-tie'-like symbol (X with horizontal bars). The latter is the one circled in the manuscript, together with F and G, and is presumably the adopted notation. Transcribing it as ≬ is approximate.
Margin note at left, opposite 'ces deux relations d'ordre': reads approximately 'ou mieux, la disjonction' (three short lines).
'[-$\ll$-] $\precsim$ de raffinement': the struck symbol looks like a crossed-out ≪-type symbol, and the retained one is ≾ (a ≺ over a tilde-like stroke).
In the NB, the struck symbol after ◇ is a filled double-headed diamond-arrow, not clearly ⇔.
